rounds.fact: The New York Times went online in 1996 and required free registration from the start, a controversial-at-the-time model that foreshadowed the paywalls most news sites use today.
Charles Schwab was one of the first traditional brokerages to fully embrace online trading, helping legitimize the idea for investors who didn't trust newer online-only upstarts.
Tripod was a major free website-builder alongside GeoCities and Angelfire, and was eventually bought by Lycos as part of its portal strategy in the late 90s.
LiveJournal was one of the first blogging platforms to build in a real social layer, with friends lists and privacy settings, making it feel more like an early social network than a simple blog host.
Vine's entire format was built around exactly 6-second looping videos, a constraint that produced its own distinct style of comedy before Twitter shut the app down in 2017.
